clue.text: Industry spurned by 11, notice, but enthralled by elastic garter

indicators.note: to be enthralled is to be held captive, so the notice sits held inside the reworked letters
something elastic stretches out of shape, so the letters of garter are pulled into a new order

parts.note: AD is short for advertisement, a printed notice

explanation.surface: A naturist sneers at an industry while a stretchy garter holds a notice in its grip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elastic' looks like a description of the garter, but it is the signal to rearrange; 'enthralled by' puts the notice inside. 11 is NATURIST, and a naturist has no use for the clothing business.
explanation.definitionFit: The rag trade is the informal name for the clothing and fashion business, which people who go unclothed ignore.

clue.text: William S's Puck, say, spurned by

parts.note: Shakespeare's Puck, in A Midsummer Night's Dream, is also called Robin Goodfellow
shortened in the style of 'William S' for William Shakespeare, Goodfellow becomes just its initial G

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's mischievous sprite is snubbed by somebody.
explanation.walkthrough: The newspaper text lost the '11' after 'spurned by'. Puck's other name is Robin Goodfellow; abbreviating the surname as 'William S' abbreviates Shakespeare gives ROBIN G. 11 is NATURIST, who scorns putting on clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Robing is dressing in a gown or garments, the very thing a nudist declines to do.

clue.text: Very good Second in University exams

parts.note: great is a casual word for very good

explanation.surface: A student praised for a fine second-class result in their degree.
explanation.walkthrough: Greats is the informal name for the final classics exams at Oxford University.
explanation.definitionFit: At Oxford, the final examinations in Literae Humaniores (classics) are traditionally called Greats.

clue.text: Crikey! — surrounded by red tape

indicators.note: something surrounded by a word sits inside it, so the exclamation goes into red

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like crikey

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in exasperation at being trapped in bureaucratic red tape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red tape' reads as one idea, bureaucracy, but RED is the container and 'tape' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A record can mean a recording, and a tape is one medium for a recording.

clue.text: The skill of clobbering yourself?

parts.note: clobber is British slang for clothes, so clobbering yourself means dressing yourself, and the skill of doing that well is having taste in clothes

explanation.surface: A question about a talent for beating oneself up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clobbering' looks like hitting, but clobber is British slang for clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a good eye for choosing flattering, stylish clothes is described as a talent for outfits.

clue.text: Drinks spurned by 11

explanation.surface: A naturist turns down alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Shorts are small measures of spirits, and also short trousers, a garment a nudist goes without.

clue.text: Interval — a couple of examples would have me backing it

definitions.text: Interval — a couple of examples would have me backing it

parts.words: Interval — a couple of examples would have me backing it
parts.note: an interval in a match; split the word for a period into two halves and the halves are 'it' turned round followed by 'me', so two examples of a half of that word put me behind it

explanation.walkthrough: The word for a period, cut in two, gives TI and ME: the first half is IT reversed and ME comes behind it, so a couple of examples of a half of that word are 'me backing it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Half-time is the break or interval between the two halves of a sports match.

clue.text: Middle of area handles places for meditation

indicators.note: the middle of a four-letter word is its central two letters, so take the centre of area

parts.note: to handle something is to deal with or treat it

explanation.surface: In the central part of a region, someone manages quiet havens for contemplation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'handles' looks like a noun, but it is a verb, meaning deals with or treats.
explanation.definitionFit: Retreats are secluded places people withdraw to for prayer or meditation.

clue.text: 11, portrayed movingly?

parts.note: 11 is a nude person; shown in motion, such a person is one who dashes naked across a public place such as a sports pitch

explanation.surface: A nudist depicted in an emotional, touching way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movingly' suggests emotion, but here it means in motion: a nudist on the run.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who runs naked through a crowd or across a pitch is the moving counterpart of a nudist.

clue.text: Openings, we hear, spurned by

indicators.note: something we hear is spoken, so the word for openings stands for one that sounds the same

parts.note: breaches are gaps or openings, as in a wall

explanation.surface: Gaps that someone rejects, by reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: The newspaper text lost the '11' after 'spurned by'. 11 is NATURIST, who rejects trousers of any kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Breeches are knee-length trousers, a garment a nudist would refuse to wear.

clue.text: Province spurned by 11

explanation.surface: A naturist snubs a region of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulster is the northern Irish province, and also a long heavy overcoat, which a nudist does without.

clue.text: One barely seen, in a rut, struggling beside the way

indicators.note: beside places one piece directly next to the other, here the street abbreviation coming after
words struggling are writhing about, so the letters of in a rut are thrown into a new order

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A person glimpsed fleetingly, stuck in a rut and struggling beside the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barely seen' sounds like hardly visible, but it means seen bare, without clothes. 'struggling' makes NATURI from IN A RUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudist is someone who is seen without clothes, in the bare state.

clue.text: Goddess getting consistently good ratings?

parts.note: A is the top grade, a good rating
consistently here means one after another, so the link between the two grades is then
a second A grade, as the plural ratings implies more than one

explanation.surface: A deity who keeps earning high marks from the critics.
explanation.walkthrough: Consistently good ratings are an A, then another A: read the goddess's name as three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Athena is the Greek goddess of wisdom and war.

clue.text: Parties set to be energised — 11's favourite act?

indicators.note: letters energised are stirred up and set moving, so these are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A party crowd is about to be livened up by a nudist's preferred performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be energised' rearranges PARTIES SET. A naturist would approve of a performance that ends in nudity.
explanation.definitionFit: A striptease is a performance of gradually removing clothes, which a naturist would naturally favour.

clue.text: Period spent penetrating core a little way

indicators.note: one piece penetrating another goes inside it, so the period sits within the core

parts.note: the core of something is its centre
time is a period, especially one passed or spent

explanation.surface: A stretch of time spent boring into a core, but not getting far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little way' is a short distance; a centimetre is a small measure of length.
explanation.definitionFit: A centimetre is a hundredth of a metre, a short distance.

clue.text: A blockage to cables being moved

indicators.note: letters being moved are shifted about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Something gets in the way of cables as they are relocated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being moved' rearranges TO CABLES.
explanation.definitionFit: An obstacle is an obstruction, something that blocks the way.

clue.text: Point to a warning spurned by 11?

parts.note: a pin is a slender sharp point
fore is the warning cry shouted on a golf course

explanation.surface: Someone indicates a caution notice that a nudist ignores.
explanation.walkthrough: FORE is the shout golfers give to warn people in the path of a ball. 11 is NATURIST, who rejects this apron-like garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinafore is a sleeveless dress or apron, an item of clothing nudists shun.

clue.text: 11's invitation to superfluous activity? I don't know

explanation.surface: A shrug of ignorance from someone who has nothing to hide.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudist inviting a frisk, pointless since nothing can be concealed, and a casual phrase of ignorance.

clue.text: Trouble is brewing round one spurned by 11?

indicators.note: the reworked letters go round the single letter, enclosing it
something brewing is being stirred and mixed, so these letters are churned into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Trouble is coming, and it is gathering around someone a naturist rejects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewing' rearranges TROUBLE IS, and 'round' wraps those letters about I. 11 is NATURIST, who shuns overalls.
explanation.definitionFit: A boiler suit is a one-piece overall worn for dirty work, a garment that nudists avoid.

clue.text: Button, round one, turning up in TV venue

parts.note: a stud is a fastener like a button, as on a shirt collar

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the letters are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: O is round in shape
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A button, making its first round, appears in a television setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses O and I into IO, following STUD.
explanation.definitionFit: A studio is the room where television programmes are filmed.

clue.text: Nobleman's timeless weapon

indicators.note: timeless means without time, and T is the abbreviation for time, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: a shotgun is a firearm, a weapon

explanation.surface: An aristocrat's enduring weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timeless' looks like everlasting, but it says remove T (time) from SHOTGUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A shogun was a hereditary military ruler of Japan, a lord of high rank.

clue.text: Ruler's charge, capturing knight

indicators.note: capturing means taking prisoner, so the knight is held inside the charge

parts.note: a charge is a price asked
N is the chess abbreviation for knight

explanation.surface: A monarch's attack takes a knight, like a chess move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' suggests an attack, but here it is a fee.
explanation.definitionFit: A prince is a ruler, as of a principality.

clue.text: Shock about English article in samovar

indicators.note: one piece about another surrounds it, so the shock goes round the other letters

parts.note: a turn is a sudden shock, as in giving someone a turn
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone is startled at an English item found inside a Russian kettle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock' is TURN, as in 'you gave me a turn'.
explanation.definitionFit: A samovar is a Russian metal urn for boiling water to make tea.

clue.text: Embroidery expert embroidered shirt etc

indicators.note: a story embroidered is elaborated and changed, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A skilled needleworker decorates shirts and the like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embroidered' rearranges SHIRT ETC.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who stitches is a sewer, and a skilled one does embroidery.

clue.text: Act unlike 11, unwilling to enter church

indicators.note: a piece made to enter another goes inside it

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
loth means reluctant or unwilling

explanation.surface: Behave differently from a naturist, reluctant to go into church.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 is NATURIST: to dress is the opposite of what a nudist does.
explanation.definitionFit: To clothe is to dress, which a nudist does not do.

clue.text: Understand one will follow vehicle spurned by 11

indicators.note: the understanding and the one come after the vehicle, as followers

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
dig is slang for understand
an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: Get it: someone will trail a car that a naturist rejects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Understand' is the slang DIG ('you dig?'). 11 is NATURIST, who rejects knitted jackets.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardigan is a knitted buttoned jacket, a garment unwanted by nudists.

clue.text: Left back not half still in soccer team

indicators.note: back means the letters are turned round, read backwards
not half means only half of the word is kept, its first two letters

parts.note: even means still, as in 'even more'

explanation.surface: A left-back plays half a game while still in a football side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left back' looks like the football position, but 'not half' keeps LE of LEFT and 'back' turns it into EL.
explanation.definitionFit: A football side fields eleven players.

clue.text: Give up reduction in rent on cue, after manipulation

indicators.note: manipulated letters are handled and rearranged into a new order
a reduction makes the word shorter, here losing its last letter

explanation.surface: Give up a cut in rent timed to the cue, after some scheming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduction in' cuts RENT to REN; 'after manipulation' rearranges REN with ON CUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To renounce is to abandon or formally give up a claim or belief.
